title: Europe capitals six of six · Iberia and the Mediterranean
edition: Europe capitals · Six regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to the Europe capitals, episode six of six. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
Four capitals close the series: the two of the Iberian peninsula, the old capital of the Mediterranean, and the smallest of the island capitals.

states.name: Madrid
lines: Madrid stands on the Manzanares river in the centre of Spain, on a plateau about 650 metres above the sea.
From Arabic al-Majrit, "source of water": the Moorish fortress was named for its streams, and the Christians kept the name.
Remember Madrid as the source of water and the highest capital in Europe at 650 metres, with the Prado holding Spain's finest painting.

states.name: Lisbon
lines: Lisbon, called Lisboa in Portuguese, stands on the Tagus river on Portugal's west coast, where the river meets the Atlantic.
Probably Phoenician Alis Ubbo, "safe harbour", though the Romans preferred a legend about Ulysses founding it.
Remember Lisbon as the safe harbour, and the city whose 1755 earthquake led to the first scientific study of an earthquake anywhere.

states.name: Athens
lines: Athens stands in the south of Greece, in the Attic plain, close to the Saronic Gulf.
Named for the goddess Athena, who in the myth won the city from Poseidon with the gift of an olive tree.
Remember Athens as the olive tree won from Poseidon, the Parthenon above the city, and the first modern Olympic Games in 1896.

states.name: Valletta
lines: Valletta stands on a peninsula on Malta's north-east coast, in the middle of the Mediterranean.
Named for Jean de Valette, grand master of the Knights of Saint John, who held Malta against the Ottomans in 1565.
Remember Valletta as the city of the grand master who held Malta in 1565, and one of the smallest capitals in the European Union.

recap: Madrid and Lisbon are the two Iberian capitals, Athens the old one of the Mediterranean, and Valletta the island capital off Sicily.
Remember the source of water, the safe harbour, the olive tree of Athena, and the grand master who held Malta in 1565.
